findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple missed hand washing opportunities:
1) One employee touched their hat, and donned a new pair of gloves without hand washing.
2) Another individual wearing gloves pulled up their pants and returned to food prep.
CORRECTED- times to wash hands were reviewed with the person in charge (PIC), who stated two new employees are on the line. An educational handout was provided by the inspector. Review times to wash hands with all employees, including, but not limited to: after touching ones self, after touching a cell phone, after handling money, after handling cleaning products, after taking the garbage out, and after changing tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a phone with an active screen on the drive thru prep counter. CORRECTED- the phone was removed from the area, and food contact surfaces were sanitized. Ensure phones (and any items that may introduce contamination to foods or food contact surfaces) are kept separate from areas of food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple wet mop heads in the basin of the mop sink. Ensure mop heads are placed in a position that allows for air drying, to prevent the harborage and growth of bacteria.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility in need of more frequent cleaning:
1) FIRST REPEAT: A significant accumulation of debris on the wall directly beneath the triple sink. 
2) The floor in the bakery storage area contains an accumulation of food debris.
Ensure the physical facilities are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand contact surface of tongs touching a baguette. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the tongs into a separate container and discarded the baguette. Ensure all utensils are stored in a manner that prevents bare hand contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:

1) Cooler drawer of cook-line facing dining room.
2) Cooler drawer of cook-line facing back of house.
3) Cooler drawer of drive thru sandwich prep cooler. A piece of metal on the right side is loose and able to obscure the ability of a drawer to close.
4) The top interior of the microwave on the cook-line.
Ensure all equipment is maintained in proper repair. Repair or replace equipment by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a ready to eat (RTE) bagel sitting on the counter at the drive through at the end of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed a need for food grade container or packaging with the PIC. The bagel was removed from service. Ensure all RTE foods are only in contact with sanitized utensils, clean gloved hands, single service containers, or napkins to prevent the contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.

1) Multiple employees were donning gloves without handwashing first.
2) An employee was handling cash with their gloves hands used for food preparation. 
CORRECTED- The person in charge (PIC) was notified about the violations during the inspection and will be educating staff about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that employees always wash hands after sources of contamination.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.

Ensure that all single service utensils are displayed in a manner that will prevent contamination of the food contact surface.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation or food residue or dust during today’s inspection.
1) FIRST REPEAT The dry storage shelving to the left of the ice machine was observed to be soiled with dust. 
2) THIRD REPEAT: Food debris was observed inside drawer coolers in the drive thru salad station and the under-counter coolers on the main cook-line.
Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as needed to prevent accumulation of food debris, dust, and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed multiple nonfood contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris;
1) There was an accumulation of soil debris around the outlets of the decaf and light roasts coffee makers in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the person in charge wiped the outlets with a clean sanitizer rag to remove debris. 
2) The microwave (particularly the top of the interior) contained an accumulation of grease and food debris. Education was provided to the person in charge (PIC) regarding the need to include cleaning and sanitizing the entire interior of the microwave on a regular basis. 
Nonfood contact surfaces and equipment should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspectors observed the outer surface of the door to the walk-in cooler to be rusted and corroded. Rust and corrosion is not considered a smooth, easily cleanable surface, and is therefore at risk of cross-contamination. Ensure the walls and door of the walk-in cooler are repaired (recommend sanding and repainting) prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- Multiple food handler’s certificates for onsite employees were observed to be expired. The person in charge (PIC) was informed that the certificates need to be renewed. Ensure all employees have a valid food handler’s certification prior to next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed sliced tomato in the walk-in cooler and prep cooler to be past its “discard by” date. The tomatoes in the walk-in were marked to be discarded on 3/10/2025, and the tomatoes in the prep cooler were marked to be discarded on 3/9/2025. The tomatoes were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are checking the date marking on all produce at the end of each day and discarding any out of date produce. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed spray bottle stored in chemical storage area to be filled with a clear liquid and no label. Informed PIC that all chemicals need to be clearly labeled to prevent toxin contamination of a food contact surface. PIC discarded contents of spray bottle. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Active roach population was once again observed around the water heater. Roaches were observed after moving a carpet sweeper away from the water heater. The carpet sweeper was removed from the facility and discarded per management’s discretion.  Roaches were also observed after removing old glue traps from the floor on the left side of the water heater. Detail cleaning and additional treatment are needed in this area. **See general comments for additional information.**
NOTE: The remains of dirty mop water was observed in mop buckets. PIC discarded used mop water. Ensure all mop water is emptied in the mop sink when no longer needed as this is a water source for pests. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Dish machine was being used without the presence of sanitizer upon arrival of inspector. Also, an active roach population was observed, and cleaning is lacking in several areas including where roaches were observed. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at follow-up inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer bucket connected to the dish machine was empty. PIC discovered this after running a cycle to check sanitizer and observing a concentration of 0ppm. Providing a fresh container of sanitizer and priming the chemical line allowed for a proper concentration of 100ppm. Prior to doing this the dish machine was being used without the presence of sanitizer. Ensure managers on all shifts are checking chemicals and verifying proper concentration for dish machine sanitization, especially at the start of operations daily prior to staff doing dishes. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

An old drain hose underneath the thermolizer next to the ice machine had roaches running out of it when moved. Old drain hoses were removed from the facility and discarded. Detail cleaning is needed in the back of the facility, especially where roach activity was observed. PCO was just out for service and on-site prior to inspector’s arrival today. Ensure cleaning throughout the facility, focusing efforts in the back kitchen, dish area, and around water heater. Call for additional service with PCO before follow-up inspection. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1) Floors were in general soiled under equipment throughout the back kitchen, dish area, and front make line. 
A. Single service articles, food debris, and general accumulation of soil were observed under the ice machine and thermolizers where roach activity was observed. 
B. Buildup of general grime and random items were observed around the water heater where roach activity was observed.
C. Heavy buildup of general debris was observed along the wall behind the dish machine.
D. Heavy buildup of general debris and other items were observed beneath the coffee counter and handwashing sink to the left of the 3 part sink.
E. Food debris was observed along walls and in corners under shelving in the walk-in cooler.
F. General buildup of food and debris was observed under coolers.
Thoroughly clean the floors throughout the facility. Ensure detail cleaning to eliminate potential food sources for roaches.

2) Wall at dish area was soiled with general buildup behind the dish machine and beneath the 3 part sink. Attached plumbing at 3 part sink was also soiled with buildup of splash. Ensure cleaning of walls throughout as needed to eliminate buildup.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Wet mop was observed in the basin of the mop sink. Ensure proper storage of wet mops between uses to allow mop heads to dry properly.
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.114 (A) Old, unused salad chiller was observed in the back of facility by chemical storage. Unused equipment can serve as a hiding place for pests. Remove unused equipment from the premise.
The premise shall be free of items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: Employee was observed rinsing their hands with the sprayer at the 3 part sink after changing out garbage can liners and just prior to returning to ware washing. Proper handwashing at designated handwashing sink was discussed. Employee washed hands at the handwashing sink prior to continuing with ware washing.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.
If hands need to be rinsed, then they should be properly washed.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee working in dish area washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with a reminder to dry hands with paper towels prior to using the paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet in order to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Ice machine had a chunk of black debris that appeared to be mold in the ice bin on the right side wall. Napkin was used to remove the debris. Covers were removed from the ice maker, and mold was observed on surfaces around water lines. The area where mold was observed was directly over an opening adjacent to the ice bin. Manager cleaned and sanitized the area where mold was observed during the inspection.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Wild rice soup in the front service line hot holding unit had an internal temperature of 127F. Soup was discarded and replaced with fresh product.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Greens and cheese slices in the Turbo Chef drive thru cooler were observed at 46F-50F. Based on information provided by the employee working in the area the cooler stopped working properly ~20 minutes prior. All TCS foods were moved to the drive thru salad and sandwich prep coolers that were holding foods below 40F.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Turbo Chef drive thru cooler was not on and had TCS foods inside (see #22 for details). Employee working in the area told the manager the light indicating power was on to the unit went out about 20 minutes prior. The cooler would not turn on. All foods were moved to properly functioning coolers. Cooler in question will not be used for storage of TCS foods until it is repaired and able to maintain foods at 41F/below. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Sanitizer solution in sanitizer-bucket at front service line was observed to be soiled from use. Solution was replaced. Ensure sanitizer solution is changed as needed throughout the day once the solution becomes soiled and/or the concentration weakens.
Chemical sanitizing solutions in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of food debris and visible soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 1. (REPEAT) Food debris and splash were observed in the bottom of coolers throughout, especially in the prep coolers. Clean inside coolers daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.
2. Shelving in both walk-in coolers were soiled with general buildup and debris. Manager noted the shelves are on the schedule to be cleaned.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12  1. (REPEAT) Wall at dish area was soiled with general buildup behind and around clean equipment storage, behind the dish machine, and beneath the 3 part sink. Ensure cleaning of walls throughout as needed to eliminate buildup. 
2. (REPEAT) Holes of various sizes were observed in the wall behind a storage rack to the left of the walk-in freezer. Repair options were discussed. Provide repairs that result in a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
3. Floors under and behind the dish machine and thermolizers were in need of cleaning. General buildup and debris accumulation were observed. Cleaning behind the thermolizer began during inspection.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen awareness certification was available for one of the three CFMs on duty during the inspection. The manager with allergen training would be leaving as of 6pm at which time the facility will not have a CFM on-site with the required training. Manager noted other CFMs are in the process of completing certification. CFMs need to complete allergen training by next routine inspection to ensure there is always someone on-site during hours of operation with the certification.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: Employee was observed rinsing their hand with the sprayer at the 3 part sink. Handwashing at designated handwashing sink was discussed. Employee washed hands at a handwashing sink prior to continuing with their next task. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.
If hands need to be rinsed, then they should be properly washed.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Hot TCS foods in the front service line hot holding unit were observed with internal temperatures below 135F. French onion soup and chili were observed at 117F and 123F, while sausages were observed at 125F. Sausages were discarded and replaced with fresh product. Soups were placed back in the thermolizer to reheat prior to hot holding for service. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12  1. Wall at dish area was soiled with general buildup behind and around clean equipment storage, behind the dish machine, and beneath the 3 part sink. Ensure cleaning of walls throughout as needed to eliminate buildup. 
2. Holes of various sizes were observed in the wall behind a storage rack to the left of the walk-in freezer. Repair options were discussed. Provide repairs that result in a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer at the 3 part sink dispenser was once again observed at improper concentration. Concentration observed for freshly dispensed sanitizer was at ~170 DDBSA/452 lactic acid. The effective concentration range for the product in use is 272-700ppm (DDBSA)/704-1875ppm (lactic acid). Sanitizer is also available at the dispenser by the mopsink. A spray bottle prepared using the mopsink dispenser was observed at a proper concentration of 700 DDBSA/1875 lactic acid. GM called the technician to request additional service for the dispenser located at the 3 part sink. The sanitizer at the 3 part sink dispenser does not consistently dispense at the proper concentration. The dispenser at the mopsink will be used for all sanitizer solutions until the dispenser at the 3 part sink is functioning properly and dispensing product at effective concentration required for use (see general comments for additional information).
If a chemical sanitizer other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. If a chemical sanitizer is generated by a device located on-site at the food establishment it shall be used as specified in ¶¶(A) -(D) of this section and shall be produced by a device that is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Management was unaware the dish machine and sanitizer dispenser at the 3 part sink were not functioning properly until inspector pointed out the issues. Management was also unable to answer questions about the sanitizer that is now in use at the facility. A switch was made from quat sanitizer to a sanitizer with active ingredients of DDBSA and lactic acid (see general comments for additional information). Management was advised as to active managerial controls and being able to demonstrate knowledge related to equipment and chemicals used at the facility. A re-inspection will occur on 6/14/21 to verify proper function of the dish machine and sanitizer dispenser at which time the demonstration of knowledge pertaining to these items will be addressed. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handwashing sink by coffee makers in back had a dark roast coffee dispenser in the basin. Coffee dispenser was removed from the basin.  
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of handsinks for any reason.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine was observed with a sanitizer concentration of 0ppm chlorine. Sanitizer bucket connected to the machine was full to the top and appeared new. Management was unsure as to when the chemical was changed, possibly the evening prior or sometime during the current operating day. After priming the line for several minutes and running additional cycles, the sanitizer concentration remained at 0ppm. Call for service was made, and a technician would be on-site the following day for repairs. In the meantime, the dishes could be washed in the dish machine and manually sanitized at the 3 part sink.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

Sanitizer was not properly dispensed at the 3 part sink dispenser. The lid was damaged on the chemical line, and suction was lacking. Even when sanitizer suctioned through the line and was dispensed it was observed at 0ppm. Sani-buckets and containers with ready to use wiping cloths registered at 0ppm DDBSA/lactic acid. Sanitizer was removed from the dispenser and mixed by hand to allow for proper concentration of 272-700ppm (DDBSA) and 704-1875ppm (lactic acid). Management was advised on mixing sanitizer by hand at the 3 part sink to use for manual sanitization until the dish machine is repaired and functioning properly.
If a chemical sanitizer other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. If a chemical sanitizer is generated by a device located on-site at the food establishment it shall be used as specified in ¶¶(A) -(D) of this section and shall be produced by a device that is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

Containers with ready to use sanitizer wiping cloths were observed to be dry. Proper maintenance of ready to use wiping cloth containers was discussed. Ensure solutions are maintained in containers and proper concentration for sanitization is available. 
If a chemical sanitizer other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 Dishes on drying racks in the dish area were not properly sanitized due to the lack of sanitization at the dish machine. All dishes were to be sanitized manually at the 3 part sink. All utensils and equipment were to be washed in the dish machine and manually sanitized at the 3 part sink until the dish machine was repaired and allowing for proper wash, rinse, and sanitize.
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112 Thermometer was not present in the barista cooler. Ensure functioning thermometers are present in all cold holding units. 
Cold or hot holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Sanitizer solution by barista station was murky and contained food debris. Solution was discarded and fresh sanitizer was provided. 
Chemical sanitizing solutions in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of food debris and visible soil. Ensure sanitizer solution is changed as needed throughout the day once the solution becomes soiled and/or the concentration weakens.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Food debris and splash were observed in the bottom of all prep coolers as well as in the currently unused catering cooler. Clean the aforementioned coolers.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen awareness certification was not available for CFMs on duty at the time of inspection. Managers noted they took the allergen course. Copies of allergen certifications need to be maintained on-site.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: Employee in dish area was observed attempting to use a prep sink for the purposes of handwashing after being advised to wash hands between handling soiled and clean dishes. Employee was advised on handwashing at designated handsinks only. Employee washed hands at the designated handsink located at the opposite end of the dish area prior to proceeding with handling clean dishes. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Freshly prepared sani-bucket on the front service line was observed at 0ppm quat. Chemical container connected at the dispenser at the 3 part sink was observed empty, and the suction line was without product. New container of quat chemical was connected to the dispenser and observed at 200ppm when dispensed. All sani-buckets were changed and replaced with fresh product at proper concentration. 
Container with ready to use wipes was observed at less than 150ppm at the drive thru and was removed from the area. The container had a use by date of 12/7/20. Another container with ready to use wipes at the front counter (register area) was observed at 200ppm and made more recently (use be date in January 2021). Management was advised to monitor concentrations and maintain fresh product in ready to use wipe containers. Management was also encouraged to train all staff on basic troubleshooting and understanding what to look for regarding basic/proper function of the quat dispenser.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.
